Chapter 1: Waking Up to a Minefield

Lin Chuxia's eyes snapped open, and a whole novel's worth of plot crammed itself into her brain.

She remembered working overtime until three in the morning, falling asleep at her desk—the standard 996 grind, straight-up corporate drone life. Now she was sprawled on a two-meter-wide European-style bed, a crystal chandelier gleaming overhead, the scent of sandalwood swirling in the air.

“Ding—System activation successful.”

A translucent blue panel materialized before her eyes:

[Welcome to the world of *The Alpha CEO's Stand-in Bride*.
Host: Lin Chuxia.
Identity: Secretary to the President of Gu Group.
Main Quest: Win over target character Gu Moyan. Return to original world once Favorability reaches 100.
Current Favorability: -20.]

Lin Chuxia stared at that negative twenty and almost choked.

“What the hell? I transmigrate and you start me at negative twenty?!”

She rolled out of bed, bare feet sinking into the wool carpet, and walked to the floor-length mirror. The reflection showed a face identical to her own but polished to three levels of perfection—skin like a freshly peeled egg, a waist so slender you could circle it with both hands.

The door burst open.

A man stood in the doorway, sharp in a crisp suit, his features as coldly sculpted as if chiseled from ice. A system label automatically popped into Lin Chuxia's mind: [Gu Moyan, 29, CEO of Gu Group, net worth in the hundreds of billions, famously nicknamed the “walking iceberg.”]

“Secretary Lin,” his voice rumbled low enough to make any ASMR fan pass out. “Are you ready with today’s board meeting merger proposal?”

Lin Chuxia froze. What proposal? She’d just transmigrated!

“Ding—Triggered Rookie Quest: Present the merger proposal. Reward: Favorability +5. Failure Penalty: Public humiliation, Favorability -10.”

Mentally, Lin Chuxia cursed the System’s ancestors eighteen generations deep, then she dragged in a deep breath and straightened her spine.

“Mr. Gu, the proposal is right here.”

She grabbed the folder off the nightstand—the original owner had pulled an all-nighter on it—and handed it over.

Gu Moyan flipped it open, his brow creasing faintly as his gaze swept across the dense data. Finally, he lifted his eyes to her—like he was inspecting a piece of disposable decor.

“Barely passable.”

He snapped the folder shut and turned to leave. At the door, he paused.

“Next time, don’t answer the door in your pajamas.”

The moment the door clicked shut, Lin Chuxia looked down at her spaghetti-strap nightgown, and her face went instantly crimson.

On the system panel, Favorability jumped from -20 to -18.

Lin Chuxia gritted her teeth. “Two points? That’s all I’m worth?!”

Outside the window, the sprawling metropolis known as Cloud City blazed with lights. What she didn’t know was that inside his car, Gu Moyan was staring at her photo, lost in thought—the woman in the picture was a seventy-percent match for the fiancée who’d vanished in a car accident five years ago.

His thumb traced the edge of the photo, his eyes darkening.

“Is it you…?”

---

Lin Chuxia spent the whole night sorting through the original owner's memories.

The original owner was also named Lin Chuxia. Orphanage background, paid her way through college on scholarships, and landed a job at Gu Corporation's secretarial department six months ago. In the original novel, she was nothing but a disposable stand-in—after Gu Moyan's white moonlight fiancée Su Wanqing disappeared in a car accident, he found a woman who looked like Su Wanqing and put her right next to him as his secretary. Torment her, then fall for her. The usual.

"This plot is way too cliché," Lin Chuxia muttered to herself over a bowl of instant noodles. "Classic CEO romance novel tropes: the stand-in, the car accident, the amnesia, the bun-in-the-oven-and-she's-gone, the getting-promoted-because-of-the-baby..."

Ding — System notification: Host analysis skill +3. Bonus reminder: Altering the original plot awards extra reward points.

Lin Chuxia slurped a noodle. "So I can't follow the original story? I have to rewrite the script myself?"

The system didn't answer, but she got the message. If she played the stand-in role according to the original plot, she'd end up framed by the sanctimonious side character Shen Ruyu and meet a miserable end. To get home, she had to bend this Bad End into a Happy End.

The next day, Lin Chuxia clicked into Gu Corporation Tower on seven-centimeter stilettos.

The lobby's massive screen scrolled today's industry headlines: "Xingchen Technology Announces Series C Funding, Valuation Breaks Ten Billion" "Gu Corporation to Acquire Huaxing Real Estate, VAM Agreement Details Exposed."

As the elevator doors were about to close, a hand shoved in and pried them open.

"Wait! Wait!"

A girl with her hair in a messy bun and a canvas bag slung over her shoulder squeezed in, nearly knocking Lin Chuxia over.

"Chuxia! Why didn't you reply to my WeChat yesterday?" Zhao Xiaobei panted. "Do you know I was looking for you all night?"

Lin Chuxia looked at the baby-faced girl and her mind pulled up the original owner's memories — Zhao Xiaobei, college roommate and best friend, the only person who knew all her secrets.

"My phone died," Lin Chuxia lied smoothly. "What are you doing at Gu Corp?"

"I'm here for an interview!" Zhao Xiaobei waved her resume. "Marketing department. If we end up at the same company, I'll be your personal popcorn gallery every day, watching you and CEO Gu's drama."

"What drama?"

"The whole company's buzzing — they say you're CEO Gu's little fling." Zhao Xiaobei lowered her voice. "And some people say you're a stand-in for his missing fiancée... But girl, we don't do backup. You deserve to be loved for real."

Ding — the elevator arrived. The doors slid open, and Gu Moyan stood right outside, sharp in his suit, flanked by seven or eight executives.

The space went dead silent for three seconds.

Gu Moyan's gaze swept over Lin Chuxia's face, landed on Zhao Xiaobei, then came back to Lin Chuxia.

"Secretary Lin. Ten o'clock, we're going to Xingchen Technology to discuss the VAM agreement. Don't be late."

Then he strode away, the executives falling in line behind him.

Zhao Xiaobei poked her head out of the elevator and whispered, "Girl, I believe it now. The way that man looks at you — there's a story."

Lin Chuxia didn't reply, because she'd just noticed something: the corner of a photo sticking out of Gu Moyan's suit pocket. The edges were worn and faded, like they'd been touched over and over again a thousand times.

Who was in that photo?

On her system interface, a new mission prompt flickered.

---

**Chapter 3: The Goody-Two-Shoes Has Thorns**

Gu Corp occupied floors 36 through 48 of the Cloud Summit Tower. Lin Chuxia's desk was on the 47th floor, just a glass door away from Gu Moyan's office.

She'd barely set down her bag when a hot latte appeared on her desk.

"Secretary Lin, you must be tired. I brought you a coffee."

The speaker wore a Chanel suit, her chestnut waves cascading over her shoulders, her smile as warm as the first ray of spring. A system tag popped up: **[Shen Ruyu, 28, heiress of Shen Real Estate, Gu Moyan's childhood friend, original novel's villain: a White Lotus (fake sweetheart). Current affinity: -50.]**

Lin Chuxia nearly choked on her own saliva. -50? What had she done?

"Thank you, Miss Shen," Lin Chuxia said, maintaining her professional smile. "But I brought my own breakfast."

Shen Ruyu's smile didn't crack, but a flicker of coldness flashed in her eyes.

"Chuxia, you've been here six months, right?" Shen Ruyu sat down across from her, her tone dripping with concern like a big sister. "I heard the secretarial department is downsizing. If you're worried, I can put in a good word with Moyan—after all, I've known him since we were kids. That counts for something."

Translation: Your job is at my mercy. Better pack up and leave.

Lin Chuxia blinked. "That's very thoughtful of you, Miss Shen. But Mr. Gu just told me yesterday that my M&A proposal was well done."

Shen Ruyu's fingers tightened around her coffee cup.

*So this is what an epic takedown feels like?* Lin Chuxia thought. *Damn, it's satisfying.*

"Oh, Miss Shen," Lin Chuxia added with a sweet smile, striking the final blow, "I think your lipstick got on your teeth."

Shen Ruyu's composure finally broke. She stood up, her smile barely holding. "I have a meeting to go to."

The moment she left, a message from Zhao Xiaobei popped up on Lin Chuxia's phone.

**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** I PASSED THE INTERVIEW!!!! I'm starting tomorrow!!!!
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** I heard in the break room that Shen Ruyu went to see you. You okay?
**[Lin Chuxia]:** Don't worry, your girl's got a secret weapon.
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** ??? What secret weapon?
**[Lin Chuxia]:** ...Nothing. I'll explain later.
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** Fine. Anyway, hotpot tonight. Your treat!
**[Lin Chuxia]:** Why me?
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** Because you're the Alpha CEO's woman! We popcorn gallery folks are just waiting for a free meal!

Lin Chuxia smiled and put down her phone—only to see a new system notification:

**[Hidden Quest Triggered: Shen Ruyu has launched her 'Rumor Campaign.' Mission Objective: Defuse the crisis within 48 hours. Reward: Affinity +10, Unlock Skill: 'Business Insight.']**

She looked up toward the conference room. Beyond the glass wall, Shen Ruyu was leaning in to whisper something in Gu Moyan's ear, but her eyes were fixed straight at Lin Chuxia through the glass.

That look held unmasked hostility.

Lin Chuxia took a deep breath. *Alright. Time-travel plus system plus alpha CEO plus White Lotus—I'll accept all of it.*

*But this game? I'm not here to play backup.*

---

"There's a problem with the core terms of this venture agreement."

Lin Chuxia stood in the conference room of StarLight Tech, facing the opposing company's legal team and CEO. Gu Moyan sat to her right, his face unreadable.

Lu Ziang sat across the long table. Thirty years old, gold-rimmed glasses, with a smile that made the spring breeze look cold. System tag: [Lu Ziang, 30, CEO of StarLight Tech, self-made tech entrepreneur. Personality: nice guy. Current affection: 10.]

"Gu Moyan, my company's revenue has grown three hundred percent over the last three years," Lu Ziang said, tone mild but firm. "There's no way I'm accepting your offer of a hundred million valuation and fifty-one percent equity. This isn't a venture agreement. It's highway robbery."

Gu Moyan leaned back in his chair, expression indifferent. "You barely squeaked past your Series A and B milestones. Now you're chasing a ten-billion valuation in Series C, but you're short on cash. Otherwise, you wouldn't have invited me to talk."

Silence filled the room, broken only by the hum of the air conditioner.

Lin Chuxia quickly flipped through the documents in her hands. Her predecessor had done thorough homework the night before—compiling the other side's financial reports, industry trends, even Lu Ziang's personal entrepreneurial history. But soon she spotted a problem: The Gu Group had undervalued StarLight Tech's patents. Their AI algorithms had seven international patents, market benchmarked at least three hundred million.

She hesitated, then quietly on the notepad under the table wrote a line and slid it to Gu Moyan.

Gu Moyan glanced at the note. His eyebrow moved so slightly it was almost imperceptible.

"However," Gu Moyan suddenly spoke, "I can revise the terms to thirty percent equity plus one board seat."

Lu Ziang froze. His legal team froze. This offer was far more reasonable than the first, even generous.

"Why the sudden change?" Lu Ziang asked.

Gu Moyan looked at Lin Chuxia, his gaze lingering for a moment.

"Because someone reminded me your patents are worth three hundred million."

Lu Ziang followed his gaze to Lin Chuxia, a hint of amusement in his eyes behind the gold-rimmed glasses.

After the meeting broke up, Lu Ziang walked over to Lin Chuxia and handed her a business card.

"Ms. Lin, interested in coming over to StarLight Tech? Double your salary, no 996 grind."

Gu Moyan came up behind her and snatched the card from her hand.

"Mr. Lu, poaching my people right in front of me?"

"Your people?" Lu Ziang smiled. "Let me rephrase—Ms. Lin, if you ever feel unhappy at Gu Group, feel free to contact me."

Gu Moyan's face darkened.

And on Lin Chuxia's system interface, two messages popped up simultaneously:

[Affection: Gu Moyan +5 (Current -13)]
[Affection: Lu Ziang +8 (Current 18)]
[Achievement Unlocked: Office Rivalry (Bronze Tier)]

---

That night after her affection score hit -13, Lin Chuxia had a dream.

She stood in a white void, facing a giant transparent screen. A flat electronic voice echoed in her ears:

"Hello, host. I am Transmigration Assistance System No. 2046. Due to your positive score in your previous life, you have been selected to participate in this transmigration experience. Clearance condition: Raise the target's affection score to 100. Enjoy your stay."

"Enjoy my ass!" Lin Chuxia shouted into the void. "You start me at negative twenty and say 'enjoy'? Why don't you just throw me into a Heavenly Tribulation right now?"

The system paused for three seconds.

"Additional note: Host can earn points by completing daily tasks. Points can be exchanged for items in the System Shop. Currently available items: 'Love at First Sight Perfume' (200 points), 'Business Prophecy Book' (500 points), 'Mind Reading: Time-Limited Edition' (1,000 points). Current points: 0."

Then the void vanished, and Lin Chuxia woke up.

Dawn was just breaking outside the window. She lay in bed thinking for a long time—this wasn't the world she had originally lived in. Here she was just a substitute, a pawn, a side character who could be crushed by the original story plot at any moment.

But if the system had given her a cheat, then she wasn't just a side character.

She rolled out of bed and opened her laptop. She had stayed up late last night reading the original novel—the original Lin Chuxia died in Chapter 87 after Shen Ruyu framed her with a fake drunk scandal, got her kicked out of the company by Gu Moyan, and finally perished penniless.

To survive, she had to change the plot.

To win, she had to make Gu Moyan truly fall in love with her, not just see her as a stand-in.

But that was harder than fighting a performance agreement. Because that man's heart was like a rock frozen in ice—hard, cold, and dead weight.

Her phone screen lit up—a message from Zhao Xiaobei.

【Zhao Xiaobei】: Girl! Wake up yet!
【Zhao Xiaobei】: I dug up all of your Mr. Gu's gossip news. Major discovery!
【Zhao Xiaobei】: His missing fiancée, Su Wanqing, was last seen at the airport holding a ticket to the US. A lot of people say she didn't disappear—she bailed of her own free will.

Lin Chuxia stared at the screen, her heart racing.

If Su Wanqing had run away on her own, then Gu Moyan's motive for finding a substitute wasn't nostalgia—it was revenge.

And her role in this story, from the very beginning, was set to impossible mode.

---

**Chapter 6: Greenhorn at Gu's Group**

On her first day at Gu's Group, Lin Chuxia learned a hard truth: in the Cloud Tower high-rise, the 996 grind was nothing compared to the office politics—and the pretentious assholes in their power suits.

"Secretary Lin, Mr. Gu's meeting minutes need to be compiled before eleven. Format must follow the company template exactly—font size 12, line spacing 1.5, and all appendix charts must be vector graphics."

"Secretary Lin, Mr. Gu has a lunch meeting with CEO Li of Huaxing Real Estate at noon. The private room at Junyue Hotel is booked. You need to arrive thirty minutes early to order—Mr. Gu doesn't eat cilantro, no organ meats, and only steamed seafood."

"Secretary Lin, have you printed the board meeting materials for three o'clock? Twenty copies, double-sided, bound in blue folders, labels on the top-right corner—not top-left, not bottom-right, top-right!"

For three straight days, Lin Chuxia felt like she wasn't just working as a secretary—she was surviving a heavenly tribulation.

The senior secretary leading her was named Liu, in her early forties, wearing reading glasses, and always kept a tight-lipped expression. The Gu's Group secretarial department had ridiculous rules—from paper weight to meeting seating arrangements, from who presses the elevator button first to the coffee machine usage priority in the break room. Everything was documented in a thick handbook.

"Our Gu's Group is one of China's top hundred enterprises," Team Lead Liu adjusted her glasses. "The CEO's secretary is the face of the company. You have decent credentials, but you still have a lot to learn."

Lin Chuxia nodded obediently, but inside she was screaming: I'm a 985 grad and a corporate drone being bossed around by a middle-aged aunty? This transmigration experience is worse than my original 996 grind.

At lunch, Zhao Xiaobei brought cafeteria lunch boxes up to the 47th floor.

"Still alive?" Zhao Xiaobei stuffed a chunk of braised pork into Lin Chuxia's mouth.

"Barely," Lin Chuxia mumbled through the meat. "But I'm about to ascend."

"Count your blessings," Zhao Xiaobei rolled her eyes. "I got assigned to the busiest team in the marketing department. Guess who the team lead is? Shen Ruyu's cousin. And guess what she made me do today? I compiled a three-hundred-page competitive analysis report, and then she said—do it over."

Zhao Xiaobei bit into a chicken leg viciously. "One day when I make it big, first thing I'm doing is making Shen Ruyu and her cousin experience what real wage slave blessings feel like."

Lin Chuxia laughed at her, but then suddenly paused. "Why is Shen Ruyu's cousin in the marketing department?"

"Family connections," Zhao Xiaobei lowered her voice. "Shen's Real Estate is a major partner of Gu's Group. Shen Ruyu herself holds a deputy director title in the PR department, but she does squat. The Shen family has three generations of ties with the Gu family. Basically—they're the arranged marriage pool."

Lin Chuxia suddenly understood why Shen Ruyu's favorability toward her was negative fifty.

In Shen Ruyu's eyes, the secretary position was the VIP express lane to Gu Moyan's bed.

And Lin Chuxia was standing in her way.

---

**Chapter 7: Hotpot, Lies, and a Missing Fiancée**

Friday night, 7 PM. Zhao Xiaobei dragged Lin Chuxia to an old-school Chongqing hotpot joint on the south side of Cloud City.

"I did some digging," Zhao Xiaobei said between mouthfuls of tripe, her eyes watering from the spice but her mouth never stopping. "Gu Moyan and Su Wanqing's story is more twisted than any soap opera."

"Su Wanqing is the only daughter of the Su Pharma family. The Su and Gu families go way back—childhood friends. They knew each other since kindergarten, started dating in college. Perfect match. Childhood sweethearts. Five years ago, on the day of their engagement, Su Wanqing's car drove off a cliff on the way to the ceremony. They never found her."

"The police ruled it a missing person, not a death," Lin Chuxia cut in. "So why does everyone act like she's dead?"

"Because they found her handbag at the bottom of the cliff. Inside was the engagement ring and a note that said—'I'm sorry.'" Zhao Xiaobei put down her chopsticks, her usual teasing grin gone. "Chuxia... you look a lot like her. I don't know if that's a good thing or a bad thing."

Lin Chuxia said nothing. She quietly dunked a slice of pork aorta into the bubbling broth.

The restaurant buzzed with noise—a nearby table played a drinking game, waiters wove through the crowd with trays, the air thick with the scent of red chili oil and Sichuan peppercorns. But Lin Chuxia felt a chill run through her.

"And that Shen Ruyu," she asked. "Was she close to Su Wanqing?"

Zhao Xiaobei snorted. "Acted like her BFF on the surface. But you can read between the lines. After Su Wanqing disappeared, Shen Ruyu was the first to post a tribute—a long, heartfelt essay about their sisterhood. Guess what she wore to the Gu family's banquet the very next day? A red dress."

Lin Chuxia remembered a passage from the original novel—Shen Ruyu's ultimate goal was to marry into the Gu family. Su Wanqing had been her first obstacle. Lin Chuxia was the second one she hadn't planned for.

*Ding—System notification: Side quest unlocked. Key clue: Su Wanqing's disappearance. Exploration progress: 10%. Reward: Unlock 'Memory Fragments' ×3 upon completion.*

The system's electronic voice echoed in the noisy restaurant, like an ice cube dropped into the bubbling red oil base.

Lin Chuxia blinked, startled. When she looked up, she saw two men walk through the entrance.

Gu Moyan and Lu Ziang.

Two men at the top of Cloud City's business food chain, wearing expensive bespoke suits, heading toward the private rooms. Gu Moyan's gaze swept casually across the main hall—and stopped on Lin Chuxia.

Lu Ziang spotted her too. He walked over with a grin. "Secretary Lin. What a coincidence. Mind if we join you?"

Gu Moyan didn't say a word, but he didn't stop Lu Ziang either. He just stood there, looking at Lin Chuxia, his gaze heavy and dark like a bottomless sea.

Under the table, Zhao Xiaobei stomped on Lin Chuxia's foot and whispered, "Bystanders with popcorn, at the ready!"

Lin Chuxia felt her heart go through an unexpected trial by fire.

---

**Chapter 8: Two CEOs, One Hotpot**

Lu Ziang had already pulled out a chair and sat down, moving as casually as if he were walking into his own home.

"Miss Zhao, I've heard a lot about you. I read that competitive analysis you did for the marketing department—the data mining was impressive." Lu Ziang smiled at Zhao Xiaobei, his wire-rimmed glasses fogging up in the steam rising from the hotpot. He took them off and slowly wiped them clean, revealing the handsome eyes behind them.

Zhao Xiaobei flinched, and a piece of tripe dropped into her sesame oil dip. "President Lu, you know who I am?"

"Starlight Tech and the Gu Corporation are competitors. I've always kept an eye on the talent pool at Gu's."

Gu Moyan sat down across from Lin Chuxia at that moment. He took off his suit jacket, draped it over the back of his chair, undid his cufflinks, and rolled his sleeves to his forearms, revealing a set of evenly toned arms.

"President Lu, first you poach my secretary right in front of me, and now you're complimenting my employee in my presence—" Gu Moyan picked up a clean pair of chopsticks, his tone flat. "Are you here for hotpot, or are you here to stir up trouble?"

Lu Ziang laughed. "I'm here for hotpot. Hotpot's a funny thing—eating it alone is boring, just two people is too intimate, but three or four is just right. Don't you think so, Miss Lin?"

Lin Chuxia could feel the gunpowder in the air. Two men whose combined net worth topped a hundred billion were locked in a silent duel over a pot of spicy broth. And she was the dish about to be cooked through.

"Um," Zhao Xiaobei bravely broke the silence, "maybe we should order first? The goose intestines here are amazing—"

"Miss Zhao," Lu Ziang suddenly turned to her, "any interest in joining Starlight Tech? Director of New Media Operations, salary based on your expectations."

Zhao Xiaobei's mouth fell open.

Gu Moyan picked up a slice of fatty beef, dipped it into the boiling broth for exactly seven dips up and down, then placed it into Lin Chuxia's bowl.

"Try it," he said.

The entire table went silent.

Lin Chuxia stared at the beef in her bowl, then looked up at Gu Moyan—his expression hadn't changed at all, as if feeding his secretary a piece of meat was the most normal thing in the world.

But she noticed: Gu Moyan's dipping technique was precise—exactly seven dips up and down, the way Su Wanqing had always liked it in the original novel.

He was looking through her, doing this for someone else.

"Ding — Affection Rating: Gu Moyan +3 (Current: -10). Warning: Stand-in dynamic triggered. Affection fluctuation increased. Risk of affection regression."

Lin Chuxia picked up the beef and took a bite.

"Not bad," she said with a smile. "But President Gu, I actually prefer ten seconds in the broth with a dry spice dip."

Gu Moyan looked at her. Something shifted in his eyes.

It wasn't that his affection went up—it was that, for the first time, he truly saw her. Not as a shadow of Su Wanqing, but as Lin Chuxia.

Zhao Xiaobei watched the drama unfold, barely containing her grin as she mentally munched on popcorn.

And Lu Ziang adjusted his glasses, his gaze flickering between Lin Chuxia and Gu Moyan. The curve of his lips was loaded with meaning.

---

**Chapter 9**: Break Room Survival 101

Monday, 8:30 AM. The 47th-floor break room at Gu Group was gossip central.

Lin Chuxia was filling her mug when three female coworkers started buzzing about her.

"You know Lin Chuxia? Last week she went to StarLight Tech with the CEO. Word is she talked back to him in front of everyone."

"I heard it wasn't talking back—she threw herself at him. You should've seen how she handed him that note—"

"She looks like her, don't you think?"

"Like Miss Su? Now that you mention it… So the CEO keeps her around for that reason?"

"A stand-in. Just wait—Shen Ruyu won't let her get away with it."

Lin Chuxia leaned against the wall outside the break room, coffee in hand, and listened to the whole tea-spilling session without interrupting. She wasn't new to office politics—back in her original world, gossip of this caliber barely broke a sweat.

But the problem was this wasn't her original world. It was a novel. And in novels, workplace gossip had a nasty way of triggering plot points.

Sure enough, at 3 PM, a post exploded on the company intranet.

**Anonymous**: SHOCKER! CEO's secretary Lin has an 'intimate relationship' with Mr. Gu—hotel photo included!

The photo was taken last week when Lin Chuxia and Gu Moyan went to Junyue Hotel for a business lunch. The angle was sneaky—cropped out the client representatives, leaving only the two of them walking into the hotel entrance.

*Ding! Crisis event triggered: Shen Ruyu's 'Rumor Plan' has been activated. Current company reputation: Negative (-30%). Mission countdown: 36 hours.*

Lin Chuxia took a deep breath and clicked on the comments.

"I knew it. How else could an orphan girl land a spot in Gu Group's executive office?"
"Disgusting. She's just using her face to climb."
"Feel bad for Mr. Gu. Stuck with a woman like her."
"Miss Shen is a thousand times better."

Her phone buzzed. Zhao Xiaobei's message came instantly:

**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** HOLY SHIT!!! Who the hell posted that?!!!
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** Wait there, I'm going to IT to trace the IP!!!
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** Never mind, I don't have IT clearance… Screw it, I'll find someone!

**[Lin Chuxia]:** Chill. I've got this handled.
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** How?! You're not a miracle worker!
**[Lin Chuxia]:** I'm not a miracle worker, but I've got a golden finger.
**[Zhao Xiaobei]:** You're talking about that golden finger thing again! Are you running on fumes?!

Lin Chuxia didn't reply. She opened the system's shop interface and found the item she needed:

**[Truth Eye · Basic]** (100 points): Reveals a hidden surveillance record. Current points insufficient. Free beginner use available—1 use remaining.

She tapped "Use."

Thirty minutes later, an anonymous IP address was pinpointed and pushed to her phone screen. Using the original body's IT skills—she'd taught herself coding back at the orphanage—she reverse-traced the device info and recent operation logs.

All evidence pointed to one person: Shen Ruyu, Deputy Director of the PR Department.

Lin Chuxia stared at the data on her screen and smiled.

She wasn't a pushover. She was a transmigrator with a system. And in this palace drama, she was about to show the sanctimonious sweetheart what a real face-slap looked like.

---

Chapter 10: Face-Slap with Style

Lin Chuxia chose to fight head-on.

She didn't hand the evidence directly to Gu Moyan. She didn't anonymously expose Shen Ruyu either—that would be letting her off too easy. Instead, she did something far more ruthless. At the next day's departmental meeting, with the entire PR team watching, she projected the anonymous post's IP trace report, Shen Ruyu's device MAC address match data, and a comparison table of the posting time against Shen Ruyu's timecard logs onto the conference room's big screen.

"Colleagues, regarding the false information circulating on the company intranet yesterday, I'm making a public clarification here," Lin Chuxia said, her voice as steady as if she were reading a grocery list. "After verification by the tech team, the anonymous poster came from an internal network within the PR department. Director Zhang of PR, could you please confirm this IP address?"

Director Zhang, a man in his forties, stared at the data on the screen. His face turned green.

The twenty-plus people in the room fell dead silent.

Shen Ruyu sat in the second row, her makeup still flawless, but the knuckles on the hand holding her pen were white.

"This might be a misunderstanding—" Shen Ruyu began.

"Miss Shen," Lin Chuxia interrupted, her tone dripping with exaggerated politeness, "I'm not saying you posted this. But if the poster used the public Wi-Fi, could someone have stolen your work account and password? After all, the network security regulations clearly state that employees bear primary responsibility for their own account security."

What a beautiful line—I didn't say it was you, but I laid out all the evidence, and let everyone draw their own conclusions.

Zhao Xiaobei sat in the back row, her eyes wide as saucers. She furiously texted Lin Chuxia on WeChat:

【Zhao Xiaobei】: !!!!!!
【Zhao Xiaobei】: Girl, you call that a face-slap? That's grinding her face into the pavement!!!
【Zhao Xiaobei】: From today onward, you're my idol! I'll go east if you say east, west if you say west! If you tell me to hustle, I'll never slack off!

An hour later, Gu Moyan summoned Lin Chuxia to the CEO's office.

He sat behind his wide desk, holding a fountain pen, tapping the surface absently with his fingertips. The afternoon sunlight streaming through the blinds carved alternating light and shadow across his face.

"Why didn't you just give me the evidence?" he asked.

Lin Chuxia thought for a moment, then decided to tell the truth. "If I gave it directly to you, Miss Shen would have claimed I forged the evidence to frame her. But if it's presented at an open meeting, with everyone watching, she can't deny it."

"You're very clever."

"Thank you, President Gu."

"Clever people don't last long in business," Gu Moyan said, setting down the pen and meeting her eyes. "Her father, Shen Jianguo, is the second-largest shareholder of the Gu Group. You slapped his daughter's face in front of two hundred people today. Tomorrow, he'll bring your name up at the board meeting."

Lin Chuxia suddenly realized that what she thought was a brilliant comeback was actually stepping into a much bigger trap.

She wasn't just fighting Shen Ruyu. She was fighting the entire Shen family's influence.

And Gu Moyan—was he watching from the sidelines, biding his time, or…?

She looked up at the man behind the desk, searching his eyes for any flicker of emotion. But there was nothing there—dark, calm, unfathomable.

"President Gu," Lin Chuxia asked abruptly, "if I ever got in the way of your business plans, what would you do?"

Gu Moyan looked at her for a long time, saying nothing.

Finally, he said something that kept her up all night:

"You won't get in my way." He paused. "Because you're different from the others."

---

**Chapter 11: The First Official Mission**

*Ding—System Main Quest Released: Target's likability score must break past 0. Time limit: 7 days. Reward: Unlock 'Book of Commercial Prophecies' × 1. Failure penalty: Transmigration experience terminated.*

Lin Chuxia received this quest notification while organizing Gu Moyan's schedule. She glanced up at the man signing documents behind the glass door—his likability had been stuck at -10 for days. Frozen solid.

What did "transmigration experience terminated" mean? Would she go back to her original world, or just vanish from this one? The system didn't say. But she wasn't about to gamble.

"Team Lead Liu, can I add something to Boss Gu's schedule next week?"

Team Lead Liu pushed up his reading glasses. "What?"

"An on-site inspection of Huaxing Real Estate. We've done so many versions of the merger proposal, all just armchair strategies. I want to suggest Boss Gu personally check out the construction site."

Team Lead Liu set down his glasses and looked at her like she had a death wish. "You've been here how long? And you're already scheduling Boss Gu's itinerary?"

But Lin Chuxia had her plan. In the original novel, Huaxing Real Estate's construction site would have a safety incident next week. The Gu Group would be implicated because of the merger, and their stock would drop twenty points. If she could give an early warning, she'd not only save the Gu Group but also boost her likability score. That was the system's gameplay—using modern knowledge and the original plot to change the story's direction.

That afternoon, she pushed open Gu Moyan's door and laid out her idea.

Gu Moyan didn't look up. "Reasons."

"Two reasons. First, Huaxing Real Estate's last quarterly report showed a forty percent drop in construction safety investment—that's a red flag. Second," Lin Chuxia paused, "I saw your merger case from two years ago. You personally spent three days at the factory before signing. When it comes to acquisitions, I trust your gut more than the spreadsheets."

Gu Moyan finally lifted his head.

He stared at her for a long time—five seconds, ten, fifteen.

"You studied my past cases?"

"Basic secretary skills," Lin Chuxia said without flinching. "Understanding the boss's decision-making style."

Silence.

"Set it up," he said.

As she turned to leave, he added, "You're coming."

"Yes, Boss Gu."

After she walked out of the office, a system notification popped up:

【Likability: Gu Moyan +2 (Current: -8)】
【Achievement Triggered: Proactive Strike. Host has changed the original plot for the first time. Reward Points: 50.】

Lin Chuxia clenched her fist. Eight points to go. Seven days.

She opened her phone and sent a message to Zhao Xiaobei:

【Lin Chuxia】：Xiaobei, book me a lunch spot near Huaxing Real Estate's construction site.
【Zhao Xiaobei】：What's the budget?
【Lin Chuxia】：Low-key, good food, private room. I'm eating with Boss Gu.
【Zhao Xiaobei】：!!!
【Zhao Xiaobei】：Girl, you're finally making a move!!!
【Lin Chuxia】：Not a move.
【Lin Chuxia】：This is a Heavenly Tribulation.

---

The Huaxing Real Estate construction site was worse than Lin Chuxia had imagined.

Scaffolding rusted steel gray. Safety nets riddled with holes. The workers' hard hats looked like they'd been picked up at a flea market. The project manager groveled as he led Gu Moyan on a tour, rattling off phrases like "safety excellence model" and "zero-accident record." But Lin Chuxia noticed the fire extinguisher next to the entrance hydrant had expired two months ago.

She discreetly snapped a photo on her phone.

Gu Moyan said nothing the entire tour. He just walked, looked, and occasionally stopped to nudge a pile of construction material with his polished shoes. His expression stayed the same—cold. The kind of cold that made people nervous.

"Mr. Gu, as you can see, this project is in a prime location. Right next to the planned Metro Line 3 station—" The project manager was spit-flying excited.

"Why is that safety net only half there?" Lin Chuxia suddenly pointed at a seven-story building under construction.

The project manager's smile froze. "It's been windy the last couple days—the workers haven't had time to patch it—"

"No time?" Lin Chuxia's voice wasn't loud, but everyone heard it. "If a worker falls from up there, you lose a life. The compensation is over a hundred thousand. But the real cost is the Gu Group's brand reputation." She turned to Gu Moyan. "Mr. Gu, I think this project needs a reassessment of its safety standards."

The site went dead silent. The project manager's face cycled through red and white.

Gu Moyan looked at Lin Chuxia for a long moment. Then he gave an order to his men: "Suspend the merger negotiations. The safety inspection team comes in tomorrow."

Back in the car, Gu Moyan sat next to her, separated by an armrest. Outside, city streets blurred past. Inside, only the hum of the AC filled the silence.

"How did you know to look at the safety net?" he asked abruptly.

"I minored in architectural engineering in college," Lin Chuxia lied. The truth was she'd reread every chapter about Huaxing Real Estate in the novel the night before, and in Chapter 53 found one sentence: 'The safety net was only half in place, at the northwest corner of the construction site.'

"You didn't major in Chinese literature?"

"Minor." She said it without flinching.

Gu Moyan didn't press. But he turned and looked at her. This time, his gaze was different. Not scrutiny. Not comparison. Not looking through her to see someone else. For the first time, he looked at her like she was an independent, complete person.

"About your lunch suggestion," he said. "Any recommendation?"

Lin Chuxia froze for a beat, then recovered. "There's this private kitchen restaurant in the western suburbs. The owner is from Chongqing—they do spicy home-style dishes. I..." She almost slipped. "I checked the nearby restaurants before. This one has the highest ratings."

"Let's go."

That meal lasted nearly two hours. Gu Moyan barely spoke, but his chopsticks never stopped. Lin Chuxia discovered he could handle spice. And his table manners were impeccable—nothing like those cheesy CEO romance novels where the male lead says things like 'Woman, you've caught my attention.' He ate like a regular working elite who'd pulled an all-nighter and had an early morning meeting.

Then again, that was exactly who he was.

As they came out of the restaurant, the system popped up with the notification she'd been waiting for:

[Likability: Gu Moyan +5 (Current: -3)]
[Achievement: Worksite Prophet. Reward points: 100. Distance to target: 3 points.]

Lin Chuxia stared at that -3. Victory was within reach.

What she didn't know was that during those two hours of lunch, Shen Ruyu was sitting in the chairman's office at Shen Real Estate, dialing a phone number.

"Dad, I want the Gu Group's acquisition of Huaxing Real Estate blocked at tomorrow's board meeting."

"Why?"

"Because of Lin Chuxia."

Chapter 13: The Underhanded Attack at the Board Meeting

The Gu Corporation quarterly board meeting was held in the most central room on the 48th floor of Cloud Tower. Floor-to-ceiling windows offered a view of Cloud City's skyline, and inside, a twelve-meter-long African wenge wood conference table filled the space. All twenty seats were occupied by directors in business suits.

Lin Chuxia sat in the observer's seat behind and to the side of Gu Moyan, pen in hand, her meeting minutes laid out before her.

Today's agenda covered three topics: the quarterly financial report, the Huaxing Real Estate acquisition, and—what Shen Jianguo had proposed—the "HR Optimization Plan."

After Gu Moyan finished presenting the quarterly results, it was Shen Jianguo's turn to speak.

Shen Jianguo was fifty-three, with a slightly receding hairline. He was well-preserved, and his voice was calm and unhurried, but every word carried a barb.

"Mr. Gu has been in charge for three years, and Gu Corp's market cap has risen from 80 billion to 240 billion. That's certainly commendable. But—" he adjusted his glasses, "—while market cap has grown, the dilution of corporate culture also deserves attention. There have been some... how shall I put it... 'personnel incidents' recently, which have already affected employee morale."

He glanced at Lin Chuxia. Everyone's eyes followed.

A cold shiver ran down Lin Chuxia's spine. Here it was, just as Gu Moyan had warned—"Her father is the second-largest shareholder in Gu Corp. He'll bring up your name at the board meeting."

"An executive secretary who's been on the job for less than a year publicly challenges the work of a PR colleague during a department meeting," Shen Jianguo continued, his tone as if stating an indisputable fact. "As a member of the president's office of a publicly traded company, is this behavior appropriate? I recommend that HR re-examine the qualifications for the executive secretary position."

The room fell silent. Some directors exchanged glances, others stared at their computer screens. No one spoke up for her.

Lin Chuxia's fingers tightened around her pen. In her mind, she frantically called the system: Is there any item I can use?

[System Reply: Current points 150. Available for exchange: 'Temporary Eloquence Boost' (100 points) or 'Business Logic Analysis' (150 points). Exchange?]

"I understand Mr. Shen's concerns."

It wasn't Lin Chuxia who spoke—it was Gu Moyan.

He leaned back in his chair, his posture relaxed, as if discussing what to have for lunch tomorrow. But his voice cut through the entire room.

"But I'd like to correct a factual error in Mr. Shen's account. What Secretary Lin did at that department meeting was not 'challenging a colleague' but assisting in an investigation into a violation of the company's internal cybersecurity regulations. The IP tracking report was officially certified by the tech team yesterday. The data is authentic."

He pulled a document stamped with the tech department's official seal from his folder and slid it to the center of the conference table.

"As for Secretary Lin's qualifications—" Gu Moyan scanned the directors around the table, "—her entrance exam and written test scores were the second highest in the secretariat's history. Since she started, she has participated in two M&A projects, and the error rate on her due diligence reports is zero percent. Those figures are available in the HR system. Feel free to check if you're interested, Mr. Shen."

Shen Jianguo's face changed color.

But Gu Moyan wasn't done yet.

"Let me propose a more practical agenda item instead," he said, interlocking his fingers on the table. "Miss Shen has been in the position of Deputy Director of PR for sixteen months. In those sixteen months, the PR department has handled seven crisis incidents. Only one was successfully managed. I deeply value my long-standing friendship with Ruyu, but the boardroom isn't a place for personal favors—it's a place for results."

He had just ripped open Shen Ruyu's wounds in front of everyone.

Lin Chuxia was stunned.

Meanwhile, the system's notifications were going wild:

[Likability: Gu Moyan +8 (current +5)]
[Likability has broken past zero! Main quest complete! Reward: 'Business Prophecy Book' ×1 issued.]
[Achievement unlocked: A Knight in Shining Armor (but not a hero, it's an Alpha CEO).]

Lin Chuxia stared at that green +5, her heart pounding like she'd just run an eight-hundred-meter dash.

Her negative score was gone. In this world, she had finally earned a foothold.

---

"Drinks! We need drinks, for real! This calls for a celebration!"

Zhao Xiaobei slammed a bottle of beer onto the table, foam splattering onto Lin Chuxia's sleeve. They were in Zhao's forty-square-meter rental apartment, the coffee table buried under takeout containers — spicy crawfish, grilled skewers, duck necks, and a lopsided cake with chocolate frosting that read "Congrats on the Epic Takedown."

"So he actually went after Shen Jianguo in front of everyone at the board meeting?" Zhao crammed a crawfish into her mouth. "Are you sure that was Gu Moyan and not an alien wearing his face?"

"Positive," Lin Chuxia said, taking a sip from her beer can. "His face didn't twitch once the whole time, like he was reading a quarterly earnings report."

"That's badass. Now that's how a real Alpha CEO rolls!" Zhao slapped the table in excitement. "You know what? The fake CEO goes around saying shit like 'Woman, you've caught my attention' — that's just cringe. The real deal shuts everyone down with a single sentence when you need it most."

Lin Chuxia laughed so hard tears came to her eyes. But deep down, she knew it wasn't that simple.

Gu Moyan had helped her, sure, but he'd also used the opportunity to put Shen Jianguo in his place. In a place like the boardroom, every move is a power play. She wasn't some princess being protected — she was just a convenient chess piece.

"Chuxia," Zhao set down her chopsticks and looked at her with unusual seriousness. "Do you actually like Gu Moyan? For real?"

Lin Chuxia froze.

She'd never thought about it. She got close to Gu Moyan because of the system quest, because of the favorability points, because she couldn't go home without them. But "like" — that word was too heavy.

"I don't know," she said. "All I know is I have to stay close to him right now."

Zhao studied her for a long moment, then sighed. "Girl, you do you. I've got your back no matter what — whether you're trying to win over CEO Gu, CEO Lu, or an alien from Mars."

"Lu Ziang?" Lin almost choked on her beer. "What does he have to do with anything?"

"Are you really that clueless, or are you just pretending?" Zhao pulled out her phone, swiped a couple of times, and held it up.

On the screen was a news headline from three days ago: "CEO Lu Ziang of Starlight Technologies: Admires a Certain Employee at Gu Group — Not Ruling Out Poaching." The photo showed Lu Ziang being interviewed at some business forum, looking mild-mannered in a light gray suit.

"A 'certain employee' — who do you think that is?" Zhao raised an eyebrow.

Lin Chuxia let her head thunk into the sofa cushion.

This transmigration world was way too complicated. She hadn't even finished the male lead quest, and the second male lead was already muscling in on the drama. She was just a corporate drone trying to finish her mission and go home — why did she have to be dragged into this love triangle hell?

The moon outside the window was big and full. Zhao was playing an old song — "The Moon Represents My Heart."

Lin Chuxia lifted her head from the cushion and stared at the moon. A sudden thought struck her: if the favorability ever hit 100, could she really bring herself to leave?

Right now, she didn't have an answer.

**Chapter 15:** The System's Hidden Rules

【Congratulations, host. Your favorability score has hit zero for the first time. Tutorial level unlocked: Detailed System Rules.】

Late at night, Lin Chuxia lay in bed. The system panel in front of her transformed into a holographic tutorial interface.

A chibi-style robot appeared on the panel and began explaining in a flat, electronic voice:

"Hello, host. I am the artificial intelligence assistant for Crossworld Assistance System, unit number 2046. You can call me 'Xiao Liu'—Little Six. I will now explain three hidden rules."

"First: Favorability is not linear. 0–30 is the 'Like' phase, 30–60 is the 'Heartthrob' phase, 60–90 is the 'Deep Love' phase, and 90+ is 'Until Death.' Breaking into each new phase requires a key plot trigger. Daily tasks can only make small adjustments within your current phase."

"Second: The 'inertia' of the original storyline. Every time you change the original plot, the world will generate counterforces—both opportunities and dangers. You helped Gu Group avoid the Huaxing Real Estate crisis, so the Shen family's counterforces have already been activated. The bigger your change, the stronger the backlash."

"Third, and most important: Favorability is not one-way. Once your target's favorability reaches 60 or above, your own emotions will be synced and bound by the system. In other words, when his heart beats for you, yours might start beating for him too—whether you like it or not."

Lin Chuxia froze. "Wait, what? So you're telling me that one day I won't be able to tell if I actually like him, or if the system is just twisting my feelings?"

"Correct."

"Are you fucking kidding me? This is a scam!"

"Supplementary note," Xiao Liu's electronic voice droned on, completely unfazed. "The System Store has an item called the 'Heart of Truth.' It can be purchased before favorability reaches 60. This item removes the emotional sync binding, allowing you to maintain independent self-awareness. Price: 3000 points."

Three thousand points. She only had one hundred and fifty.

"One more question," Lin Chuxia said. "If I fail—if favorability drops to zero or a negative event brings it into the red—what happens to me?"

"The travel experience terminates. You will be sent back to your original world. Note: If the experience terminates after favorability exceeds 60, the emotional sync will not be cleared. You will return to your world carrying your feelings for him, while he remains in this world, forever out of your reach."

Lin Chuxia dismissed the system panel and lay in the darkness, eyes wide open, unable to sleep for a long time.

She finally understood: this system wasn't designed to help her fall in love. It was designed to extract pain from her.

Behind every point of favorability lay a no-win trap. Score too low and you can't go home. Score too high and you break yourself. Every step forward in this world was a tightrope dance.

And the person holding her safety rope? There might not be one.

Thunder rumbled outside. June in Cloud City had entered the rainy season.

---

**Chapter 16: The Entrepreneur's Gentleness**

As Lin Chuxia surfaced from the haze of fifteen late nights working until dawn, a friend request popped up from an unfamiliar ID.

The profile picture was a side shot of Lu Ziang standing by the ocean. The handle was "CStar·Lu." She hesitated for a few seconds, then accepted.

**[Lu Ziang]:** Miss Lin, are you free this afternoon? I'd like to invite you for coffee. Don't misunderstand—it's business.

**[Lin Chuxia]:** What kind of business?

**[Lu Ziang]:** Xingchen Technology is attending the China AI Industry Summit next month, and we need an industry white paper. I heard the industry analysis reports you did at the Gu Group were excellent. I'd like to hire you as a consulting advisor. Paid, of course.

**[Lin Chuxia]:** I work for the Gu Group. Isn't it inappropriate for me to take freelance work from a competitor?

**[Lu Ziang]:** That's why I said "consulting advisor," not "full-time employee." I've read the Gu Group's non-compete agreement—it doesn't restrict providing professional consulting services. Of course, if you're not comfortable, I understand completely.

Lin Chuxia stared at the screen for a long time. This guy was meticulous—every sentence gave her an easy way to say no, but also paved a path for her to say yes. No wonder everyone called him a cinnamon roll.

She thought it over and typed back:

**[Lin Chuxia]:** Saturday, 3 PM, The Study Room Cafe in the Guomao Center. You're buying.

**[Lu Ziang]:** Deal.

Saturday afternoon, Lin Chuxia pushed open the glass door of The Study Room Cafe and saw Lu Ziang already sitting by the window. He wasn't in a suit today—white T-shirt under a light blue knit cardigan, looking like the most popular teaching assistant on campus.

"About the white paper," he said, pulling a stack of materials from his bag. "Xingchen Technology's AI algorithms are currently active in two tracks: medical imaging and autonomous driving. But what I'm missing is the industry landscape analysis—who the real competitors are, which direction is a red ocean trap, and where the long-term value lies."

"This counts as business?" Lin Chuxia sat down across from him. "You could easily assign this to your own strategy department."

Lu Ziang smiled, the corners of his eyes crinkling in an attractive way.

"The strategy department would only tell me what they think I want to hear. But Miss Lin—" he paused, looking at her, "you would tell me the truth. Just like that line you wrote on the sticky note in the Xingchen Technology meeting room: 'Their patents are worth 300 million.' The entire legal team missed it. You're the first person I've met who told the truth for the opponent at a negotiation table."

Lin Chuxia's heart skipped a beat. That day, she had pointed out the value of the patent to help Gu Moyan, but only because it was information that already existed in the original novel—the Gu Group had underestimated Xingchen Technology. She was just restoring facts. But in Lu Ziang's eyes, it had turned into business integrity.

"Fine," she said. "I'll take it. But I have two conditions. First, the proposal won't go through my email—I'll give you a hard copy. Second, don't think of me as anything special. We're just client and consultant."

Lu Ziang looked at her and suddenly asked an unrelated question:

"Miss Lin, are you happy working at the Gu Group?"

Lin Chuxia didn't answer.

"I'm not trying to poach you," he said with a smile. "I just think someone as smart as you shouldn't be reduced to a stand-in."

Lin Chuxia nearly dropped her coffee cup.

He knew. He knew everything—about Su Wanqing, about the stand-in role, about her situation at the Gu Group.

"How did you—"

"Cloud City is a small business world," Lu Ziang said, taking a sip of his coffee. "And I've been paying attention to you longer than you think."

The cafe played soft jazz. Sunlight filtered through the greenery onto the table, and Lu Ziang's profile looked warm and clean in the light and shadow.

All of a sudden, Lin Chuxia realized: this man was dangerous.

His danger wasn't in his strength, but in how much he paid attention to every single person.

Chapter 17: Why a Sweet Guy Hates Playing Second Fiddle

Lu Ziang's "interest" dated back three months.

That day, he was at an industry networking event at Gu Group. As the crowd was dispersing, he passed by the break room and overheard a conversation. It was Lin Chuxia teaching an intern how to fix a report—the intern had made a complete mess of the data tables and was on the verge of tears. Instead of scolding her, Lin Chuxia opened her own laptop and walked her through building a pivot table from scratch.

"I didn't learn this in school either," she said in English, then switched back to Chinese. "There's a huge gap between what they teach in school and what you actually need in the workplace. So don't be scared—take it slow."

Lu Ziang stood outside the break room, catching a glimpse of her through the frosted glass—a girl with a ponytail who didn't look much older than the intern herself, yet spoke with the calm confidence of someone who'd trained a hundred apprentices.

He started paying attention to her from that day on.

He noticed how she ate lunch alone, then quietly memorized case studies and business regulations in the stairwell. He saw her practicing English in the elevator by reciting Warren Buffett's annual letters from her phone notes. He watched her get chewed out by her team leader, take three deep breaths in the restroom, splash cold water on her face, and walk out with a perfect professional smile.

She was running as fast as she could—like something was chasing her.

"You know what I admire most about you?" Lu Ziang said at the café that afternoon. "You could totally coast on your looks, but you don't. You're fighting back against this unfair world with sheer competence. That's rare."

Lin Chuxia felt a little embarrassed, looking down as she stirred her coffee.

"Mr. Lu, did you take a course on giving compliments?"

"No course," he said, thoughtful. "I just never hold back praise for people who deserve it."

...

That evening, Lin Chuxia got back to her apartment and found Zhao Xiaobei curled up on the couch, flipping through her photo album. Zhao Xiaobei had just returned from a business trip and came straight over.

"Your coffee date with Lu Ziang made it onto the business gossip circuit," Zhao Xiaobei said, shoving her phone in Lin Chuxia's face. The screen showed an influencer post with a clickbait headline: "Alpha CEO's Stand-In vs. Tech Tycoon's Flirtation: Insider Says Secretary Lin Plays Both Sides!"

"Did Shen Ruyu put this out?" Lin Chuxia flopped onto the other end of the couch, annoyed.

"Not her. The IP traced back to someone at Huaxing Real Estate—you made a lot of enemies with that safety net project last time." Zhao Xiaobei tossed the phone aside. "Girl, you're the epicenter of Cloud City's business world storm. Gu Moyan, Lu Ziang, Shen Ruyu, Shen Jianguo—everyone's circling around you. Today you have coffee with a guy and it's trending. If you ever actually date someone, it'll be live-streamed globally."

Lin Chuxia stared at the candid photo—her and Lu Ziang sitting face-to-face in the café. Maybe it was the angle or the lighting, but both of them looked like they were smiling.

If Gu Moyan saw this picture, how many points would his affection score drop?

She picked up her phone, hesitating. Should she send him a message to explain? She stared at his WeChat profile picture—a solid white image. Just like him: clean, cold, with no clues to decipher.

Zhao Xiaobei snatched the phone from her hand.

"Don't send it. Sending it now makes you look guilty. Wait for him to ask first. This is called—game theory."

"Since when did you become an expert in game theory?"

"From reading all those alpha CEO romance novels." Zhao Xiaobei said it with a completely straight face.

**Chapter 18: Shen Ruyu's Deadly Orchestration**

Shen Ruyu sat in the private clubhouse of Shen Family Real Estate, a long, slender cigarette held between her fingers. On the low table before her were three items: a photo of Lin Chuxia, Gu Moyan's itinerary, and a photocopy of Huaxing Real Estate's safety inspection report.

"Cousin, I've dug up everything on Lin Chuxia," said the speaker—Shen Jiajia, Zhao Xiaobei's direct supervisor in the marketing department and Shen Ruyu's cousin.

Shen Jiajia was in her early twenties, with a sweet, harmless face. But every veteran in the Gu Group's marketing department knew the rule: mess with anyone but Shen Jiajia. She had the uncanny ability to identify a coworker's most cherished possession within three days, and then destroy it by the next deadline.

"Go on," Shen Ruyu said, tapping off her ash.

"Lin Chuxia, twenty-five years old. Grew up in the Sunshine Orphanage in the south end of town. She got a full scholarship to Cloud City University’s Chinese Literature program. The summer after her junior year, she hauled bricks on a construction site—literally," Shen Jiajia scrolled through her phone. "Not for some life experience kick. She needed tuition for the next semester. Before the orphanage, she had three foster families. Every single one sent her back, for one reason or another."

Shen Ruyu thoughtfully flicked her cigarette.

"What do people like that fear most?" she asked suddenly.

Shen Jiajia thought for a moment. "Falling back to the bottom. And having their past exposed."

"Exactly," Shen Ruyu’s eyes lit up. "So the way to deal with Lin Chuxia isn’t to humiliate her—she doesn’t care about that. She’s been looked down on her whole life. The real move is to make her most trusted person witness the thing she least wants revealed."

Shen Jiajia handed over a new document. "For the PR department’s annual charity event this year, I recommend the beneficiary be… the Sunshine Orphanage."

Shen Ruyu smiled. It was a very elegant, very dignified, and very terrifying smile.

She wanted to make Lin Chuxia stand beside Gu Moyan and watch the Shen Family publicly throw charity at the orphanage she grew up in. She wanted the entire company to know that the Chanel-clad secretary Lin crawled out of the slums.

And Gu Moyan’s fiancée had to be a proper lady from a noble family.

Her plan was flawless—except for two things.

First, Lin Chuxia was not the original Lin Chuxia. The original might have feared her background being exposed, but this Lin Chuxia had crawled her way up through worse in her old world. An orphanage? So what. She got into college on her own merit, earned her job, made her money—that backbone was stronger than anything.

Second, she had no idea Lin Chuxia was packing a system.

At 11:00 PM that night, Lin Chuxia received a system alert:

[Critical plot event detected: "Public Humiliation at the Charity Gala." Trigger time: Next Friday, 7:00 PM. System recommendation: Deploy countermeasures in advance.]

Lin Chuxia put down her phone and stared at the ceiling from her bed. She'd been in this world for nearly a month, climbing from -20 affinity to +5, surviving anonymous rumors and turning the tables at the board meeting. Every time she was pushed into the water, she climbed back out.

But this time, her opponent wasn't just Shen Ruyu—it was the entire Shen family behind her.

She needed backup.

---

Lin Chuxia dialed a number.

"Mr. Lu, I need your help with something. But it might put you at odds with the Shen family, so feel free to say no—"

"What is it?" Lu Ziang cut her off directly.

"Next Friday, the Gu Corporation is hosting a charity gala. Shen Ruyu is going to use the orphanage I grew up in as ammunition against me. I need someone to get there before she speaks and release a public service short film about the real situation at Sunshine Orphanage in the southern part of the city. Not handouts. Not condescending charity. I want everyone in that room to genuinely respect those kids."

There was a few seconds of silence on the other end.

"You're sure you want to steal Shen Ruyu's spotlight on the Gu family's turf?"

"I'm sure."

Lu Ziang let out a laugh—not mocking, but appreciative.

"Give me three days. Star Technology's marketing team is great at visual storytelling. I'll pull in our best director and camera crew. But—" his tone shifted, "this favor doesn't come free."

"I know. What do you want?"

"I want you. Not right now—" he paused, "I want you to promise me that if you ever decide to leave the Gu Corporation, Star Technology's door will always be open. Not as a secretary. As a partner. Your business instincts are as sharp as any investor I've met. I'm not letting that talent go to waste."

Lin Chuxia held the phone, and suddenly her nose stung.

In a world full of scheming and backstabbing, someone was willing to have her back—asking for nothing in return but a distant, future promise that might never come due.

"Okay," she said. "Deal."

"Deal."

After hanging up, the System flashed a notification:

[Side Quest: Alliance with Lu Ziang. Hidden affection triggered: Lu Ziang +15 (current total: 33). Warning: When the second male lead's affection exceeds 50, the 'Romantic Battlefield' story arc will activate, making the route exponentially harder.]

Lin Chuxia took a deep breath. She knew she was walking an increasingly narrow tightrope. But to ruin Shen Ruyu's scheme, she was willing to take the risk.

Three days later, Lu Ziang sent the first cut of the short film. Watching it alone in her apartment, Lin Chuxia couldn't stop the tears from falling.

The film didn't include a single line begging for pity. The camera simply documented daily life at the orphanage—kids doing homework together, eating together, running on the shabby playground. The old director looked into the lens and said one thing: "We don't need sympathy. What we need is for every child to be respected as a whole person."

Lu Ziang added a subtitle at the end:

"This film is dedicated to everyone who had to grow up alone from a young age. Over the next three years, Star Technology will provide free AI education platforms to all welfare institutions in Cloud City. Not as charity. So that every child has the right to choose."

"Holy shit, this isn't a charity short film," Zhao Xiaobei sent a voice message on WeChat, her voice hoarse as if she'd just been crying. "This is a f*cking nuclear bomb."

---

The charity gala on Friday night was held in the Crystal Hall of the Cloud City International Convention Center. Twelve hand-blown crystal chandeliers hung from the ceiling — each one worth more than a house. Hand-woven carpets from Iran covered the floor. A seven-tier champagne tower glittered under the lights. The air smelled of citrus and amber custom fragrance.

Every major player in Cloud City's business scene was there — real estate tycoons, tech new money, investment banking elites, and second-generation heirs of the old families. Men in tailored suits, women dripping in jewels. The social maneuvering was as precise and ruthless as a game of chess.

When Lin Chuxia walked into the ballroom behind Gu Moyan, at least half the eyes in the room turned to her. She knew exactly what those looks meant — Oh, that's the secretary who looks like Su Wanqing. That's the stand-in the boss keeps around.

Gu Moyan wore a navy custom suit tonight, his pocket square folded with military precision. He walked ahead, steady as a battleship cutting through dark currents. Lin Chuxia followed in her stilettos, maintaining the perfect distance — close enough not to seem distant, far enough not to seem clingy.

Shen Ruyu wore a strapless red mermaid gown, her makeup flawless enough to have stepped off a fashion magazine cover. She glided over with a glass of champagne, her smile soft and warm as moonlight.

"Moyan, Chuxia — you're finally here." She naturally looped her arm through Gu Moyan's. "I had Jiajia arrange tonight's charity auction. The finale is a special public interest project."

Shen Ruyu looked at Lin Chuxia, and hidden in her eyes were blades you'd miss if you blinked. "Chuxia, this project has something to do with you. You'll want to listen carefully."

Here it was. The trap Shen Ruyu had laid for her, spread out under this glittering night.

The charity auction ran for over an hour, each bid higher than the last. Then Shen Ruyu stepped onto the stage, a speech in her hand.

"Ladies and gentlemen, our final charity initiative tonight is the 'Wings of the Clouds' project, launched by the Shen Foundation. Over the next five years, we plan to fund educational institutions in all of Cloud City's impoverished communities—"

The big screen lit up with a line of text: Sunshine Orphanage in South City.

"Our first partner — Sunshine Orphanage, South City. We've learned that this facility has fallen into disrepair, and the children's living conditions are very difficult. The Shen Foundation will allocate five million RMB this year for—"

"I'm sorry, Miss Shen, but I need to interrupt."

Lin Chuxia stood up. The eyes of three hundred people turned on her like spotlights.

"Sunshine Orphanage is my home," she said, her voice soft but carrying through the hall. "I grew up there. I know every child, every teacher, every crack in the wall."

She paused, then pulled a USB drive from her clutch.

"I have a short film I'd like everyone to watch. This film was — " She swept her gaze across the room and finally locked eyes with Shen Ruyu. "...made for the children. Not as charity. As respect."

The big screen switched. The public service short film Lu Ziang had produced began to play.

Three minutes later, the entire hall was dead silent.

Not ordinary quiet — the kind of silence where something hits you in the chest, your breathing slows, and your eyes start to sting.

Gu Moyan watched the final frame — the orphanage children laughing together on the playground at sunset. His fingers tightened on his wine glass.

He turned to look at Lin Chuxia.

Her profile was half in shadow from the lights, but she stood straight. It wasn't forced strength. She simply wasn't going to shed a single tear here.

"Ding — Affection: Gu Moyan +12 (Current +17)"

"Ding — Achievement Unlocked: Returning Good for Evil (No, Face-Slapping with Truth)"

"Ding — Affection: Lu Ziang +10 (Current 43). Lu Ziang is currently in Sector B of the ballroom and watched the entire scene."

Lin Chuxia took a deep breath and looked at Shen Ruyu.

Shen Ruyu stood on the stage. Her smile finally cracked. Her goody-two-shoes mask was falling away, petal by petal, under the gaze of three hundred people.

---

The morning after the charity gala, Gu Group’s stock opened with a 4% gain.

Business media ran side-by-side headlines about "Sunshine Orphanage in the South City" and "Gu Group"—and they weren’t negative. They were glowing. The public service short film went viral on social media, with the hashtag #EntrepreneurRespect rocketing to the top of the trending chart. The most-liked comment read: "Lin Chuxia, that secretary of his—she’s Gu Group’s real brand moat."

Gu Moyan slid a folder across the desk toward Lin Chuxia.

She was standing in his corner office, still holding a freshly brewed Americano. The charity gala last night had left her with barely any sleep—the system had been chiming nonstop, various affection increases and achievement pop-ups flashing so fast it made her dizzy.

"This is this morning’s board resolution," Gu Moyan said, leaning back in his chair. "You’re appointed as Strategic Advisor to Gu Group’s Corporate Social Responsibility Department. Concurrently serving as executive secretary. A fifty percent salary increase. Equity incentives—three-year vesting."

Lin Chuxia opened the folder. Her fingers felt numb. Fifty percent? That was the kind of raise she’d have killed three years for in her original world! Transmigration, poverty or fortune—all thanks to whether the system delivered. Wait, no. It was all thanks to how hard she worked.

"Mr. Gu, I—"

"I’m not rewarding you," Gu Moyan cut her off, his voice as cool as ever. "What you did last night—the brand value you brought to Gu Group—we can’t quantify it precisely yet, but conservative estimates put it at no less than two hundred million. The company is simply giving you the basic return on that investment."

"Also," he paused, pulling another document from his drawer, "the safety report on Huaxing Real Estate is out. They’ve covered up four safety incidents over the past three years. Originally, they offered a 8% annual return on their three-year profit guarantee. Now they’ve voluntarily dropped to 12%. That one has your fingerprints all over it too."

Lin Chuxia thought of the photos on her phone—rusted scaffolding, half-torn safety nets, expired fire extinguishers. So those little details really had played a role. In the world of modern business, a single detail could be worth hundreds of millions.

A quote surfaced in her memory, one she’d read on a business finance account back in her original world: "The core of business competition is mastery over details." Back then, she hadn’t really understood it. Now, standing at the floor-to-ceiling windows of Cloud Tower’s 48th floor, overlooking the entire skyline of Cloud City, she finally got it.

"Mr. Gu," she asked, "why did you listen to my suggestion about going to the construction site in the first place? You could have just brushed it off as me sticking my nose where it didn’t belong."

Gu Moyan picked up his black coffee and took a sip.

"Because you looked like you were talking about something you knew for certain would happen." He met her eyes, a faint, almost imperceptible light in his gaze. "And in twelve years of doing business, the one thing I trust most is certainty."

That was the difference between a CEO and everyone else: ordinary people discussed feelings; high-level players calculated probabilities. And Gu Moyan had picked up on her aura of certainty—the kind of confidence only a transmigrator could have, knowing exactly what the future held.

"Go back to work," Gu Moyan said, returning his attention to signing documents. "Are you free tonight?"

"Huh?"

"Come with me somewhere."

"Where?"

"You’ll find out when we get there." He didn’t look up.

Lin Chuxia walked out of his office, her heart pounding. That man had finally started taking the initiative to ask her out.
