**Chapter 22: Gu Moyan's Secret**

At seven in the evening, a black Maybach pulled up outside the cemetery gates on the northern outskirts of Cloud City.

Lin Chuxia sat in the passenger seat, staring through the window at the pines and gray tombstones beyond the iron gate. Her heart raced. *What the hell? He takes me to a cemetery? This isn't exactly a classic move in the CEO romance playbook.*

"Get out."

Gu Moyan had already stepped out, holding a kraft paper folder. He wasn't in his suit—instead, he wore a black turtleneck and dark gray trousers, and in the fading light, he looked like the lead in a movie scene.

Lin Chuxia followed him through rows of headstones until they stopped in front of a white marble slab. Engraved on it was a woman's name—Su Wanqing. The dates of birth and death were stark; her life had ended at twenty-four.

"They found her," Gu Moyan said, his voice low. "Three months ago, in a small county in Yunnan. After the car accident, the river swept her downstream. The locals didn't think to call the police; they buried her in the village cemetery. The police did a DNA match. It's her."

He crouched down and placed the folder beside the gravestone.

"These were her belongings. The engagement ring from that day. The note—her favorite scarf." He paused. "For five years, I thought she was alive. That she just ran away because she didn't want to marry me. I don't even know if I was looking for a substitute to punish her—or to punish myself."

His voice cracked toward the end.

Lin Chuxia stood there, watching this man—usually as cold as an AI—crouch in front of his beloved's grave, his shoulders trembling slightly. Her system went haywire, emotional analysis data flooding the panel, but she dismissed all the pop-ups.

She walked over and squatted beside him, saying nothing. She just handed him a tissue.

The wind rustled through the pines in the cemetery. In the distance, Cloud City's lights began to glow. The skyscrapers of the Lujiazui financial district traced golden outlines against the dusk. The city hummed on, capital never sleeping, but in that corner of the graveyard, the two of them sat in silence for a long, long time.

"Do you know why I brought you here?" Gu Moyan stood, folded the tissue into his pocket, and resumed his cool expression—though his eyes were still rimmed red.

"No."

"Because I don't want another substitute." He turned to look at her, his eyes for the first time stripped of all barriers. "You look like her, but you're not her. Su Wanqing never had that stubborn grit you have—the way you stand your ground. When I looked at Su Wanqing, all I wanted to do was protect her. But when I watched you go head-to-head with Shen Ruyu—"

He paused.

"I wanted to applaud."

Lin Chuxia froze. The system notifications went wild:

**[Affection: Gu Moyan +15 (Current: +32)]**
**[Stage Breakthrough: Liking → Falling]**
**[Key Plot Triggered: Fall of the Substitute. Gu Moyan has let go of his obsession with Su Wanqing and begun to see you as an independent romantic interest—not a replacement.]**

Lin Chuxia felt her throat tighten. She had come into this world ready to be a hardworking strategist, a corporate drone with a system, doing missions. She wasn't ready to face a heart melting for her—a heart that had been frozen solid for five years.

"Let's go," Gu Moyan said, turning and walking toward the cemetery exit.

"Where?"

"To eat—I'm really starving." He rubbed his stomach and, surprisingly, let out a small laugh.

That was the first time Lin Chuxia saw that iceberg of a man wear such a genuine expression. Not a corporate smile. Not a negotiation-room courtesy. It was the laugh of someone who was truly hungry, a little helpless. Under the cemetery's stark fluorescent lights, he looked like a real person too.

---

After dinner with Gu Moyan that night, Lin Chuxia sat on the carpet in her apartment and opened the system shop.

3,000 points. That was the price of "True Heart" — the item that would let her maintain independent consciousness past 60 affection and stop the system from forcibly syncing her emotions. And how many did she have now? She checked her system panel:

Main storyline reward: 150
Construction Site Prophet Achievement: 100
Business Insight Unlocked: 80
Charity Dinner Reversal: 200
Affection Breakthrough to Level 32: 120
Total points: 650

Still a long way off.

But she spotted another item in the shop: 【Skill: Memory Anchor】(200 points). Description: Allows the host to retain one complete memory fragment from their original world, immune to the system's memory decay effect.

The system's memory decay effect? So she would slowly forget her original world?

She bought it immediately. Then she activated the skill, requesting "the complete picture of her life in the original world."

The system flickered for a few seconds.

【Error: Request too broad. Please specify concrete memory fragments. Example: 'mother's smile', 'first day at first job', 'a specific conversation.' Note: Host can only retain three memory fragments.】

Three. Only three. In this strange world, she could only keep three images to remind herself who she once was.

She closed her eyes and chose three anchors: her parents' faces — that family beach trip when she was twelve, her father carrying her on his shoulders into the waves, her mother laughing and taking photos. Her college graduation — waving at the camera in her cap and gown in front of the main building, Zhao Xiaobei holding a sign that said "You're the best!" in the audience. And her last day in the original world — working overtime until 3 a.m., that project that crushed her, the night she fell asleep at her desk.

Her old life had been unbearable but real. Just like the orphanage director used to say — "Keep moving forward so that one day you can look back without regret."

After locking in those three memories, she felt much more grounded. Then she realized a very practical problem: she had no ID in this world. No — the original owner had one, but that was "this world's Lin Chuxia." If she really wanted to live here —

Her phone buzzed.

【Zhao Xiaobei】: Sis, at two o'clock — no, wrong — I mean, tomorrow at 10 a.m., there's a new hire coming in. You wanna come see? Word is Mr. Gu interviewed her personally.

【Lin Chuxia】: What position?

【Zhao Xiaobei】: Secretary Team 2. Taking over your old role. You're headed to Corporate Social Responsibility now, so the Executive Secretary spot is open.

Lin Chuxia froze. She hadn't told Zhao Xiaobei about the transfer yet — looked like the HR system had already updated. There'd probably be a frenzy of gossip posts on the company intranet tomorrow.

【Zhao Xiaobei】: But the real tea isn't the new hire. It's that she looks — well — kinda like Lu Ziang's ex.

【Lin Chuxia】: …Is the gossip density in Cloud City's business district just way too high?

【Zhao Xiaobei】: Hey, our company is the boot camp for the popcorn gallery.

Lin Chuxia burst out laughing. She flopped onto the bed, massaging her slightly sore calves.

Tomorrow was a new day. And tomorrow — was her first official day in the CSR department. Her desk moved from the 47th-floor executive office to the 42nd.

Five floors away from Gu Moyan. Was that distance a good thing or a bad thing? Her last thought before falling asleep was — I hope the system's signal doesn't get blocked by concrete.

---

The next morning at ten, Lin Chuxia met the new secretary in the elevator on her way to the 47th floor to hand over her work.

The woman was about twenty-five, with shoulder-length hair, delicate features, and a very plain work skirt suit. She looked like she'd just graduated from some university in a small remote city. She pressed the button for the 47th floor, then clutched her tote bag strap nervously, her palms sweating.

"You're the new secretary?" Lin Chuxia greeted her warmly.

"Yes—hello, I'm He Yuwei. Please take care of me." She bowed so deeply she nearly hit her head on the elevator wall.

Every second in that elevator with the woman named He Yuwei gave Lin Chuxia the strangest feeling. Her manner, the way she spoke, the habit of biting her lower lip when nervous—they all reminded her of someone else. Not Su Wanqing. Not Shen Ruyu. But a name Lin Chuxia had seen many times in the original novel: Lu Ziang's ex-girlfriend.

The original had mentioned it in two sentences: "Lu Ziang dated a girl in college. She was introverted and not good with people. They broke up because of personality differences. Later, she disappeared."

Could it be her?

On the 47th floor, He Yuwei stepped out and was taken by HR toward Gu Moyan's office. Lin Chuxia stood there, watching her back, running through every clue about this character from the original novel. Then she pulled out her phone and texted Lu Ziang:

[Lin Chuxia]: A personal question—what was your college ex-girlfriend's name?

A few minutes passed before he replied.

[Lu Ziang]: He Yuwei. Why do you suddenly ask?

[Lin Chuxia]: She started at Gu's today. Gu Moyan's secretary.

A long silence. Lin Chuxia watched the "typing..." indicator flicker three times before disappearing.

Finally, Lu Ziang sent only one line:

[Lu Ziang]: She's a good person.

Lin Chuxia pocketed her phone, hugged her file box, and headed to the 42nd floor. As the elevator numbers ticked down, a stone seemed to sink in her heart.

She didn't know why He Yuwei had come to Gu's. But she remembered a hidden subplot in the original novel—Lu Ziang's business partner had once secretly betrayed him, and that person later vanished. If He Yuwei was connected to that thread...

But she didn't have energy to chase that lead now.

Her own work was waiting. The CSR department office was much more spacious than the 47th floor—larger floor-to-ceiling windows, better light, and a faint scent of locust flowers in the air.

She sat down at her new desk and looked around, then noticed a huge corporate org chart hanging directly above her seat. From left to right: all the subsidiaries of Gu's Group, departments, overseas offices—and the equity stake of Shen's Real Estate. The number made her pupils contract sharply: Shen Jianguo's stake in Gu's Group was 19%, far more than the "second-largest shareholder" she'd previously assumed. This percentage was close to the first-largest shareholder, the Gu family's 31%.

If the Shen family won over a few more minor shareholders, Gu Moyan's controlling stake would face a real threat.

She'd won the charity banquet battle, but the chess game Shen Ruyu was playing went far beyond that night. What she wanted wasn't to embarrass Lin Chuxia—it was the Gu's Group itself.

---

The first time Lin Chuxia opened the "Business Prophecy" file, she almost thought she had walked into the wrong mall.

She had expected something flashy—a glowing book, maybe, or a crystal ball full of mystical business proverbs. What she actually got was a plain gray cover with a single line printed on it: "Optimal Business Decision Guide Based on Current Variables."

She turned to the first page.

【Variable 1: Current market value of Gu's Group. Variable 2: Shareholding ratio of Shen's Real Estate. Variable 3: Series C valuation of Xingchen Technology. Variable 4: Safety inspection risk score of Huaxing Real Estate. After cross-calculation, the system generates the following three optimal strategy recommendations——】

Strategy 1: Recommend that Gu's Group make appropriate concessions on the performance-based agreement in exchange for a full rectification commitment from Huaxing Real Estate. Recommended concession: two percentage points. This will ensure long-term cooperation stability, which is more valuable than short-term profit maximization.

Strategy 2: Recommend early-stage layout of a technical partnership with Xingchen Technology—not an acquisition, but a joint laboratory. The AI space that Lu Ziang is active in has huge synergistic potential, and Gu's Group's traditional industrial resources happen to be the ideal scenario provider for AI implementation.

Strategy 3: ... (This recommendation involves sensitive business information. It can only be unlocked after the Host reaches the highest trust level with Gu Moyan.)

Lin Chuxia read through the first two strategies in one breath, feeling like her brain had been plugged into a charger. The system's analysis was razor-sharp—not only did it give recommendations, but it also explained the market data and industry trend reasoning behind each one.

She immediately turned that part into a formal proposal. At the bottom of the file, she signed her name: "Corporate Social Responsibility Department · Lin Chuxia." Then she hesitated, and added a line in parentheses below her signature: (This proposal is based on comprehensive analysis of public market data and the company's internal financial reports.)

Then she sent the file to Gu Moyan's email.

Half an hour later, Gu Moyan's reply came—not an email, but a phone call.

"Come to my office."

Lin Chuxia took the elevator to the 47th floor and walked into the CEO's office under He Yuwei's timid gaze. Gu Moyan was standing by the floor-to-ceiling window on the phone. He gestured for her to sit on the couch.

He pulled the phone away and said to the other person, "—I need to reconsider this plan. I'll get back to you—" Then he hung up and turned to face her.

"Who wrote these two suggestions?"

"I did." Lin Chuxia's heart skipped a beat. Actually, she was just the translator who turned the system's suggestions into human business language.

"The judgment on the concession range for the Huaxing Real Estate performance agreement—" He walked over to her, flipped open the file, and pointed at a line on the third page. "What data did you base this on? This level of precision prediction—I need to know your reasoning."

Lin Chuxia's mind raced. She couldn't exactly say, "An AI system from some unknown dimension calculated this." She had to come up with a reasonable explanation for the source of this knowledge.

"I helped President Lu with an AI industry white paper before—of course, as a consultant," she figured she could be honest about that part, since Gu Moyan already knew Lu Ziang had contacted her. "While working on that project, I did extensive analysis on adversarial game theory in corporate mergers and acquisitions. There was a lot of historical data analysis on valuation fluctuations—covering a wide range, referencing the latest 50 domestic M&A cases—"

Gu Moyan listened seriously, not interrupting. When she finished, he spoke.

"I'm giving you access—company business database access, highest level. From now on, you can pull in more dimensions of data for your analysis." He paused. "Also—your second recommendation, about the technical partnership with Xingchen Technology. I want to hear your more detailed thoughts."

A partnership between Gu's Group and Xingchen Technology?

The two companies had overlapping business scopes and market positioning. They were co-opetition on the same track—they could be either competitors or partners. But if they actually collaborated, the commercial landscape of Cloud City would be completely reshaped.

And Lin Chuxia saw something even bigger in it.

**Chapter 26: The Other Side of Burning the Midnight Oil**

At 10:30 that night, Lin Chuxia was the only one left on the 42nd floor. Outside the window, Cloud City still blazed with lights, like someone had scattered a handful of glowing shards across the dark blue sky. She curled her legs up in her chair and sipped her third cup of coffee in front of her laptop—she was working on the full version of that Business Prophecy report. The system had given her the core logic, but she had to fill in the supporting data, the textual presentation, and the report structure all by herself.

She was exhausted, but also weirdly wired. The high-stakes business analysis in front of her was nothing like the boring daily reports from her old job. This was way more interesting.

The elevator chimed.

Lin Chuxia assumed it was security making rounds and didn't look up. Then a cup of hot chocolate landed on her desk.

"You forgot to lock the door again."

It was Gu Moyan's voice. She looked up and saw him leaning against the side of her cubicle, jacket gone, only a white shirt on, his tie hanging loose at the collar. His face, usually as expressionless as carved ice, showed a subtle frown.

"Do you work late every day?"

"Not every day," Lin Chuxia said, picking up the hot chocolate and taking a sip — the temperature was just right. "Just today. I wanted to get this done."

"I'll look over the first draft of that partnership proposal tonight." He sat down at the workstation next to hers, also holding a cup of black coffee. They were less than a meter apart. The open office was dead silent at 10:30 p.m. — so quiet she could hear them both breathing.

Lin Chuxia typed rapidly. "Okay, President Gu. I'll try to send you the first draft tonight—"

"Wasn't it supposed to be tomorrow morning? Skipping breakfast again?" He caught her off guard with a question she didn't expect.

Her fingers froze over the keyboard. Gu Moyan — this walking business machine, this cold man who treated everyone like they were temps — was actually worried about whether she ate breakfast?

*Ding — Affection: Gu Moyan +3 (Current +35). Heart Rate Detection Activated: Host's current independent affection coefficient for Gu Moyan = 41 (unsynchronized, standalone perception). Warning: When host's independent affection coefficient exceeds 60, a system-free personal emotional bond will be triggered — independent of the system and not protected by removal items.*

Lin Chuxia almost spilled the hot chocolate. Her personal affection was already at 41? And without any system-forced synchronization?

That meant she wasn't being pushed by the system to feel something for Gu Moyan — she was developing those feelings on her own.

"What's wrong?" Gu Moyan noticed the shift in her expression.

"Nothing — just a little —" She took a deep breath. "Just some work stress."

Gu Moyan looked at her for a moment. The night light caught his profile, casting deep shadows. He reached out and tapped the edge of her screen. "Do it tomorrow."

"I can't — this report—"

"I said tomorrow." His tone didn't have the force of a command, but there was a warmth that made it hard for her to argue. "What if you work yourself to death in the middle of the night? Then who's going to make all those accurate business predictions for me?"

Lin Chuxia couldn't help but laugh. This guy even wrapped his concern in business logic. But she shut down her computer and picked up the hot chocolate anyway.

They took the elevator down together. Just the two of them, the numbers ticking down floor by floor. He stood on her left, staring at the changing digits on the elevator door. There was none of that cheesy elevator confession scene she'd seen in TV dramas. But somehow this felt more real — that between them, it wasn't one person chasing the other. They were standing side by side, heading in the same direction.

He walked her to her apartment building. She turned to go upstairs, and he stood outside for a while, looking up until the light in her apartment window flicked on.

**Chapter 27: Lu Ziang's Past**

Saturday afternoon, Lu Ziang asked Lin Chuxia to come by Starlight Tech's office to make the final edits on that industry white paper.

When Lin Chuxia arrived, she pushed open the glass door and found Lu Ziang wasn't at his desk. She called his name, then heard a dull thud from the lab—something hitting the floor.

She ran over and saw him sitting on the ground, his back against a server cabinet. A photo frame was clenched in his hand, and beside his foot lay an old phone with a shattered screen. His gold-rimmed glasses were set aside, his eyes rimmed red. That face, always wearing a warm smile, now looked like something had crushed it.

"What happened?"

He handed her the frame. The photo inside was of Lu Ziang and He Yuwei from a few years ago—the two of them laughing at the camera on a university lawn. He looked fresh as a poplar tree; she seemed like a little daisy nestled beside him. He Yuwei's features and vibe were soft and sweet—almost exactly like the nervous girl Lin Chuxia had seen in the elevator.

"She didn't come just to be a secretary," Lu Ziang said, his voice low and hoarse. "I had someone check a couple of days ago. He Yuwei worked at Shen's Real Estate for half a year last year—Shen Ruyu placed her here."

In Lin Chuxia's mind, the pieces clicked together like a puzzle. Shen Ruyu had planted Lu Ziang's ex-girlfriend beside Gu Moyan—what was the endgame here?

"What does Shen Ruyu want her to do?"

"No idea." Lu Ziang picked up the shattered phone and placed it on the table. "But I know Yuwei. She's easily scared. If someone has leverage on her, she'll do whatever they want. Her mom is a longtime employee at Shen's Real Estate—three more years until retirement when she can get her full corporate pension. Shen Ruyu is probably using that as a bargaining chip."

"So what are you thinking?" Lin Chuxia sat down next to him.

"I want to go talk to her. Not to get back together—there's nothing left between us. But I want to know what she's really afraid of. If my past ends up making the Gu family dance to Shen Ruyu's tune..." He put his glasses back on, his emotions slowly steadying. "I'd regret that."

Then he turned to look at her, his eyes complicated behind those lenses. "I appreciate your backbone, but I know most people in this world aren't like that. He Yuwei's different. When she hits a crisis, her brain just freezes up."

Lin Chuxia thought about the "Mind Reading·Limited Edition" in the system shop—it cost 1,000 points, and she was still 350 short. If she could find out what He Yuwei was really afraid of, she might be able to stop Shen Ruyu from using her.

But the world never goes according to anyone's plan.

Lu Ziang's phone rang. He picked it up, listened for three seconds, and his face changed.

"He Yuwei was on the rooftop of the building just now—she didn't jump. Security stopped her." He stood up and grabbed his jacket. "I need to go to Gu's Tower."

"I'm coming with you."

As they reached the door, he suddenly stopped.

"Lin Chuxia—thanks for not saying 'you still love each other' or 'you're meant to be' or any of that crap." He pulled the door open again, half-turned to her, his voice carrying a bone-tired sincerity. "I hate it when people try to force comfort on me. You just sitting there with me in silence—that meant more than a hundred empty words."
